correctness.rationale: All 32,767 nonzero quadratic equations, 39,997,440 compatible unordered generator pairs, 2,880 pencils through one fixed quadric, five orthogonal orbit representatives and all 31 rational hyperplanes per representative are explicitly exhausted by finite algorithms. Group action, double counting, and 105 rational-point incidences per surface validate the tables. The supplied scripts reproduce the computations.

originality.rationale: Dolgachev--Duncan classify regular characteristic-two pairs of quadrics and imply the possible surface forms; therefore that classification is expressly excluded from novelty. The new finite-field anticanonical smoothness-and-point-count spectra require exhaustive nontrivial hyperplane geometric tests, which the inspected sources do not state. Asgarli--Ghioca motivate all-smooth pencils but do not give the profile. Bergvall examines singular anticanonical sections in characteristic-zero moduli rather than exact 31-plane F2 point-count distributions. An unindexed existing numerical table remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed, unpublished, or not freely searchable finite-field computation may have tabulated the same 31-hyperplane spectra.
The general pencil-classification theory can make new numbers mechanically computable, but it does not print or directly imply their evaluated values without substantial finite enumeration.
Only searched and inspected accessible sources; novelty is best-knowledge, not certified global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Anticanonical smooth genus-one hyperplane sections are the natural finite-field Bertini locus of degree-four del Pezzo surfaces. The precise 12/15/9 spectrum and rational-point refinements separate characteristic-two arithmetic types indistinguishable by the seven rational surface points, notably disjoint elliptic rational-point ranges for two surfaces with the same discriminant partition. This is meaningful contact/arithmetic geometry, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or old pencil-classification restatement.
